narratives.Description: scope:complete refuses a code-bearing brief that has a stamped productPullRequest but no github-issue reference, so shipped PR-only work cannot complete honestly. ## In plain English
A code-bearing brief can ship through a stamped productPullRequest with no github-issue origin, then scope:complete refuses because the identity join only knows how to derive expected repo/issue from x-xbrief/github-issue. Creating a placeholder issue and editing the already-merged PR body to add Closes then passes, so the join does not prove association-at-merge. Prefer-A adds an honest PR-only completion path on productPullRequest (or x-xbrief/github-pr), warns earlier when a code-bearing brief lacks an issue origin, and judges closing-issue association as of merge time on the issue-anchored path.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. PR-only identity anchor: when resolvePlanGithubIssueRef is null and plan.metadata.productPullRequest (or an x-xbrief/github-pr reference) is present, verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity accepts that PR as the identity anchor: require --pr equals it, PR merged, merge_commit_sha equals --merge-commit, repository from evidence/--repo or default remote. Do not invent a fake issue closer requirement for that path.
2. Early disclosure (warn, not hard-refuse as v1 primary): at promote/activate or xbrief:preflight for isCodeBearingScope without issue origin, print a remediation that names the PR-only complete contract and the issue-first path, so the gap is visible before implementation. Keep promote green for intentional PR-only briefs.
3. Merge-time closer association (issue-anchored path): when an issue ref is present, reject a closingIssuesReferences membership whose connecting timeline event or body edit postdates merged_at, so a post-merge Closes edit cannot manufacture identity.
4. Keep NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS honest: do not steer delivered PR-only briefs into cancelled/superseded/experiment_archived/accepted_not_delivered to clear the gate.

## Reject (draft)
- Early hard-refuse at promote/activate as the only fix (leaves already-merged PR-only briefs stuck; breaks intentional PR-only consumers)
- Treating productPullRequest auto-discovery (#3583) as already solving identity when issue ref is absent (tip still fails)
- Closing via NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS for work that shipped
- Relying on current closingIssuesReferences alone without a merge-time association check on the issue path

## Park (draft)
- Broader forge timeline API shape beyond closing-association-as-of-merged_at
- Requiring every brief to carry a github-issue origin by policy (separate tickets promise work)
- Reworking #3675 ancestry rules already shipped

## Round 1 verdict

Prefer-A is the right direction for honest PR-only delivery, but cannot bind as written: repository authority and the positive merge-time association proof need tightening. No issue-first hard refusal is needed to resolve either gap.

Verification: pin-read only at b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0, using git show and git grep; issue body and comments through 6254595802 only. No sibling posts read. This is source/control-flow verification, not a live reproduction of GitHub's post-merge mutation behavior or an executed test suite.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: bind the repository independently of completion evidence

Evidence: [verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L539) currently derives expected repository from the plan and rejects an evidence-repository mismatch before fetching the PR. productPullRequestFromPlan in orphan-active/running-briefs.ts yields only a number. Draft item 1 instead permits repository from evidence/--repo or the default remote.

Failure: PR numbers are repository-local. For a numeric anchor N, caller-selected --repo can substitute another repository's merged PR N. Merge-SHA equality checks the substituted PR against the supplied SHA; it does not establish the intended repository. Delivery ancestry is a separate constraint and does not make repository identity unique (for example, forks can share commits).

Consequence: bind an expected (repository, PR number) tuple independently of the completion claim. A qualified github-pr reference can supply both; a numeric productPullRequest can use a canonically resolved project repository. Make --repo a matching assertion, not a competing authority. Define conflict behavior when both anchor forms exist; reject disagreement instead of silently picking one. Preserve issue-anchored validation when an issue origin exists. This is the identity/swarm boundary: identical PR numbers across repositories or worktrees must not select another unit's evidence.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: absence of a late edit is not proof of association at merge

Evidence: [ClosingIssueRef and fetch contract](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L149) carry repository and issue number only; the query at line 442 returns no association history. The verifier at lines 603–629 checks current membership. Pin searches found no ConnectedEvent/DisconnectedEvent or timelineItems implementation of the proposed historical proof.

Failure: draft item 3 says to reject membership whose connecting event or body edit postdates merged_at. A negative test alone leaves missing/unavailable history unspecified. Conversely, rejecting any later body edit rejects a legitimate pre-merge closer followed by a typo correction. An arbitrary earlier cross-reference, or a link added then removed before merge and restored afterward, is also not sufficient evidence that a closing association was effective at merge.

Consequence: require positive, repository-qualified evidence that this PR's closing association to this issue was effective at the authoritative merge time. Specify the supported evidence source and fail-closed result/remediation for unavailable, incomplete, or ambiguous history. Verify that the chosen forge surface actually exposes the required semantics before binding P3 relief. Test late introduction, valid pre-merge association with harmless later edit, removal/readdition, and missing history. Do not use caller --merged-at or mutable current body as historical authority.

Merge-time closing association is sufficient for the narrow P3 defect when it is actually proved; it is not proof of implementation correctness or immutable original brief intent. No general forge-history framework or ancestry redesign is requested here. The minimum evidence contract needed by item 3 cannot be parked with broader API design.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: cover discovery and choose one concrete early disclosure point

Evidence: [discoverDeliveryEvidenceForComplete](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/b35d8ffa8184b4dbb0f4f5d643e540517c0e67c0/packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts#L1646) skips discovery when explicit selectors exist, but at lines 1711–1724 rejects a stamped productPullRequest without an issue-derived repository. scope/main.ts advertises automatic discovery when selectors are omitted. preflight/evaluate.ts's lifecycle-ready evaluation and swarm/readiness.ts's validateCandidate have no delivery-anchor warning; the shared delivery helpers are completion consumers, not an early issue-origin requirement.

Failure: changing only verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity leaves the normal no-selector completion command failing for the same PR-only brief. Also, the draft's 'promote/activate or preflight' leaves P2's actual observable surface undecided.

Consequence: use the same anchor resolver in discovery and explicit verification, retaining existing delivery-branch/ancestry checks. Bind one named early warning point and its message/test, rather than adding gates everywhere. Explain that an anchor must be recorded by completion; a PR need not already exist at promotion. Preserve green early transitions for intentional PR-only work. A test of both explicit and selector-free completion prevents a partial P1 fix.

## F4 — footnote: confirmed baseline, honest dispositions, and envelope mismatch

At the pin, isCodeBearingScope reaches true for non-empty swarm.file_scope unless an earlier explicit non-code override applies. verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity immediately rejects a null issue reference; productPullRequest does not rescue it. The existing stored-provenance guard also uses the code-bearing classifier; it does not supply early completion-contract disclosure.

NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS really bypass delivery validation, but stamp the selected non-delivery disposition and handoffState implemented. That is not an honest delivered result. The existing remediation already says not to use --non-delivery for shipped work; P4 needs the working delivered path, not another escape enum.

The open-critique envelope/Stop 1 also includes a named refutation-target, contrary to the contract's open-charter envelope rule. I treated it as a claim to verify, not a restriction on the critique. Panel deposit matches the ceiling; sibling completeness is not observable by this critic.

## Pain coverage and strongest rejected readings

P1 is real at the pin. Prefer-A can relieve it with a qualified PR anchor plus both completion entry paths. P2 is real as a missing early disclosure, and a warning is appropriate; no issue-first gate is required. P3 remains unproved by the draft's negative timestamp sketch until F2 is resolved. P4 is relieved by honest delivered completion, not by relabeling shipped work.

Early hard-refuse is strongest when issue-first is an intentional project policy: it is simple and prevents future late surprises. It still strands already-merged PR-only briefs and contradicts the stated intentional PR-only requirement. An explicit operator change to that requirement plus an honest legacy-completion route would change my verdict.

Treating #3583 as solved is strongest because a stamped product PR already drives discovery and reuses the delivery gate. The null-issue branch before its fetch and the downstream identity join refute that reading at this SHA. A pin where both branches accept a qualified PR-only anchor would reverse it.

The non-delivery escape is strongest for genuinely abandoned, superseded, or unshipped work; it is already auditable and avoids forging merge proof. Evidence that this particular work did not ship would make that path correct. It does not solve the delivered case.

Tip at `b35d8ffa8184` still blocks honest PR-only `scope:complete`. Prefer-A draft 6254564171 closes P1–P4 without hard-refusing intentional PR-only briefs, if the successor lean tightens three under-specified limbs. ## Re-verify (pin-read)

- `verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts`): `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef(plan)` then hard-fail when null — exact #3675 no-issue-ref message. No `productPullRequest` / `github-pr` branch.

- Closing fetch: GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences(first:100){nodes{number url repository{nameWithOwner}}}` — current forge state only. No `merged_at` / timeline / ConnectedEvent filter on the membership check.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

A brief that is tracked by PR only (no `x-xbrief/github-issue` reference) can be promoted, activated, implemented and merged, and then `scope:complete` refuses it. The only way to record the delivery is to create a new issue after the fact and edit the merged PR's body to say `Closes #<new issue>`. That post-merge edit then satisfies the identity join, which shows the join does not prove what it is meant to prove.

Observed on `@deftai/directive-core` 0.125.0. The logic in `scope/delivery-evidence.js` is unchanged in 0.125.2.

## What happens

1. A consumer brief has no `x-xbrief/github-issue` reference. Its origins are spec sections, a user request and decision records. It carries `plan.metadata.productPullRequest: <n>` and a non-empty `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope`.
2. Promote, activate, preflight and readiness all pass. None of them requires an issue origin.
3. The product PR merges.
4. `scope:complete -- <active brief> --merge-commit <sha> --pr <n>` fails:
   `Delivery identity join failed: plan has no x-xbrief/github-issue reference to derive expected repository/issue (#3675).`
5. The operator's agent creates a new issue whose body says it exists only to satisfy the identity join. It binds that issue into the brief and edits the already-merged PR's body to add `Closes #<new issue>`. GitHub adds the issue to the merged PR's `closingIssuesReferences`, and completion can proceed.

## Why this is a defect

- **No PR-only completion path.** `isCodeBearingScope` returns true for any brief with a non-empty `swarm.file_scope`, even without an issue reference. `verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity` then derives the expected identity only from `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef(plan)` and hard-fails when it is null. `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` is not consulted. Every `NON_DELIVERY_DISPOSITIONS` value (`cancelled`, `superseded`, `experiment_archived`, `accepted_not_delivered`) would misrecord work that shipped. So a delivered PR-only brief cannot complete honestly.
- **The requirement surfaces only after merge.** `hasGithubIssueRef` / `resolvePlanGithubIssueRef` / `isCodeBearingScope` are used only by `scope/delivery-evidence.js`. Nothing at promote, activate, `xbrief:preflight` or `swarm:readiness` warns that a code-bearing brief will need an issue origin to complete.
- **The identity join can be satisfied retroactively.** The join checks the PR's current `closingIssuesReferences`. GitHub updates that list when a merged PR's body is edited, so a link added after merge passes. The join therefore does not prove the PR was associated with the story when it merged.

## Expected

One of these, plus the third point in either case:

1. For a code-bearing brief with no issue reference, accept `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` (or an `x-xbrief/github-pr` reference) as the identity anchor: require `--pr` to equal it, the PR to be merged, and `merge_commit_sha` to equal `--merge-commit`.
2. Or refuse early: promote/activate (or preflight) fails a code-bearing brief that has no issue origin, with a remediation that names the issue-first path, so the gap is found before implementation rather than after merge.
3. Either way, judge closing-issue association as of merge time (for example, reject a closing link whose connecting event or body edit postdates `merged_at`), so a post-merge edit cannot manufacture identity.

## Actual cost

One placeholder issue created only to satisfy the gate, a post-merge edit to a merged PR body, and an extra bind commit on the active brief before the lifecycle PR could open.

## Related

#3675 (identity join), #3583, #4864, #3791.
